subtitle: From forsaken infant to healer of kings and monks

panels.shot: epic wide of Takshashila’s terraced hills fading into Magadhan palace silhouettes
panels.action: Adult Jivaka Komarabhacca stands at the edge of Takshashila’s rocky heights, a simple physician’s satchel at his side, looking toward distant Rajagriha and a monastic grove, caught between courtly grandeur and the quiet world of the Buddha.

dialogue.text: Abandoned at birth, trained in Takshashila, Jivaka Komarabhacca rose to serve Bimbisara, Ajatashatru and the Buddha—but what kind of medicine could carry one man across kingly power and renunciant doubt?

i18n.hi: जन्म पर ही छोड़ दिया गया, तक्षशिला में सीखा, जीवक कोमारभच्चा ने बिंबिसार, अजातशत्रु और बुद्ध की सेवा की—but कौन‑सी चिकित्सा एक आदमी को राजा के बल और सन्यासियों की शंका के बीच ले जा सकती थी?

panels.shot: moody dusk wide of Rajagriha’s rocky outskirts
panels.action: On the stony ground outside Rajagriha, a newborn lies swaddled in rough cloth near the city path, while distant palace walls rise above the rocks and a few townsfolk pass by without noticing.

dialogue.text: The Vinaya tells of a child left outside Rajagriha, a royal city in Magadha. No father’s name, no clan, only a bundle on stone and the indifference of a busy road.

i18n.hi: विनय में राजगृह के बाहर छोड़े हुए बच्चे की कथा है—मगध की रजधानी। न पिता का नाम, न कुल, बस पत्थर पर पोटली और व्यस्त सड़क की बेरुख़ी।

panels.action: A woman servant in simple palace attire discovers the crying infant and lifts him gently, while in the background the outlines of Bimbisara’s palace rise in sunlit sandstone.

dialogue.text: Taken in by those near the Magadhan court, the foundling was named Jivaka Komarabhacca. His cradle stood under the shadow of King Bimbisara long before the boy understood what a king was.

i18n.hi: मगध दरबार के लोगों ने उस मिले हुए शिशु को अपना लिया। नाम मिला—जीवक कोमारभच्चा। उसका पालना राजा बिंबिसार की छाया में था, बहुत पहले, जब उसे राजा का मतलब भी नहीं पता था।

panels.shot: low-angle interior wide of the palace courtyard
panels.action: Young Jivaka, barefoot and curious, stands at the edge of a palace courtyard watching physicians examine a nobleman, their baskets of herbs and metal instruments laid out in orderly rows.

dialogue.text: Within the bustling palace, Jivaka watched healers weigh powders, feel pulses, and question the sick. In a world ruled by kings and warriors, he saw another kind of power at work—the power to ease pain.

i18n.hi: महल की चहल‑पहल में जीवक ने वैद्यों को देखा—वे पिसे औषधि तौलते, नाड़ी देखते, रोगी से पूछते। राजाओं और योद्धाओं की दुनिया में उसने एक और शक्ति देखी—दर्द मिटाने की शक्ति।

panels.shot: close mid-shot in a modest chamber
panels.action: A sympathetic elder attendant speaks to a teenage Jivaka, who stands with hands folded, listening intently, a travel bundle resting beside him.

dialogue.text: “If you wish to heal, go north, child. Takshashila trains even paupers.”

i18n.hi: “अगर सचमुच इलाज करना चाहते हो, उत्तर जाओ, बच्चे। तक्षशिला ग़रीबों तक को साध लेती है।”

panels.shot: sweeping landscape wide from behind Jivaka
panels.action: Jivaka, now a youth, walks along a caravan route toward the northwest, a simple staff in hand and a small bundle on his shoulder, as traders, ox-carts and students move along the dusty road.

dialogue.text: With little more than resolve, Jivaka joined the stream of travelers heading toward Takshashila, the famed seat of learning beyond the rivers. For one without lineage, knowledge itself would be his only wealth.

i18n.hi: थोड़ी‑सी दृढ़ता लेकर जीवक यात्रियों की धारा में शामिल हो गया, जो नदियों के पार ज्ञान‑नगरी तक्षशिला की ओर जा रहे थे। जिसे वंश न हो, उसके लिए ज्ञान ही दौलत है।

panels.action: Takshashila’s stone houses line a hill as scholars, merchants and artisans crowd the streets; Jivaka stands small among them, looking up at a teacher’s house marked by stacked scrolls and baskets of roots.

dialogue.text: Takshashila was no single university, but a city of teachers, crafts and debate. Jivaka sought a master of medicine, ready to pay not with coins, but years of disciplined study.

i18n.hi: तक्षशिला कोई एक विश्वविद्यालय नहीं, गुरुओं, शिल्प और बहसों का शहर था। जीवक ने एक महान वैद्य की खोज की, तय करके कि फीस चांदी नहीं, सालों की तपस्वी पढ़ाई होगी।

panels.action: Inside a simple teaching room, Jivaka kneels respectfully before an elderly physician seated on a low stool, palm-leaf manuscripts and jars of dried herbs arranged behind him.

dialogue.text: The Vinaya speaks of seven years under a single teacher. Jivaka learned not from abstract theory alone, but from questions, cases, and the unforgiving test of sick bodies and scarce remedies.

i18n.hi: विनय सात साल तक एक ही गुरु के अधीन रहने की बात करता है। जीवक ने सूखी थ्योरी से नहीं, सवालों, मरीज़ों और बीमार देहों व कम औषधियों की सख़्त परीक्षा से सीखा।

panels.shot: teaching-hall wide with small group of pupils
panels.action: In an open verandah, the teacher gestures to a clay model of the human body while Jivaka and other students sit attentive, baskets of roots and leaves beside them, the hillside forest visible beyond.

dialogue.text: He studied diet and regimen, diagnosis by sight and touch, and the logic of cause and effect in illness. Early Indian medicine, as preserved in Buddhist texts, mixed observation, speculation and moral concern.

i18n.hi: उसने आहार और दिनचर्या, आँख‑हाथ से पहचान, और रोग में कारण‑फल की सोच पढ़ी। बौद्ध ग्रंथों में बची पुरानी भारतीय चिकित्सा में निरीक्षण, कल्पना और नैतिकता घुली हुई थी।

panels.shot: dynamic training montage wide in the forest
panels.action: Jivaka moves through forest and hillside: examining bark, crushing leaves between fingers, digging roots, watching villagers, his satchel steadily filling with specimens under shifting light.

dialogue.text: Medicine meant knowing the land. Day after day, Jivaka walked Takshashila’s hills, handling each plant, linking local knowledge with formal training, until the terrain itself became his textbook.

i18n.hi: चिकित्सा ज़मीन से जुड़ी थी। रोज़‑रोज़ जीवक तक्षशिला की पहाड़ियाँ नापता, हर पौधे को छूता, गाँव की जानकारी को शिक्षा से जोड़ता, जब तक कि पूरा भू‑भाग ही उसकी पाठशाला बन गया।

panels.action: By oil-lamp light, Jivaka sits alone with palm-leaf manuscripts, making careful notes, his brow focused, bundles of dried herbs hanging behind him in the darkened room.

dialogue.text: “If I fail the sick, who will speak for them?”

i18n.hi: “अगर मैं बीमारों को निराश कर दूँ, तो उनकी आवाज़ कौन बनेगा?”

panels.shot: daytime forest wide with teacher and student
panels.action: On a wooded slope, the teacher stands with arms folded while Jivaka listens; dense undergrowth, shrubs and trees surround them, sunlight cutting through leaves.

dialogue.text: “Bring me a plant that has no use in medicine, Jivaka.”

i18n.hi: “जीवक, मुझे कोई ऐसा पौधा लाकर दिखाओ जिसका औषधि में कोई काम न हो।”

panels.shot: low tracking wide of Jivaka moving through varied terrain
panels.action: Jivaka searches high and low: on rocky outcrops, wet stream banks, scrub and tall trees; he pauses often, examining each plant with a mixture of hope and doubt.

dialogue.text: It seemed a simple test. Yet the more Jivaka searched, the more uses he recalled—poultice, decoction, purgative, soothing balm. Practical knowledge and belief wrapped every plant in potential healing.

i18n.hi: परीक्षा आसान लगी। पर जितना जीवक ढूँढ़ता, उतनी यादें जगतीं—लेप, काढ़ा, विरेचक, मलहम। हर पौधे के चारों तरफ़ अनुभव और विश्वास का एक इलाज लिपटा था।

panels.action: Jivaka returns to his teacher at the forest’s edge, hands empty but posture firm, the hillside stretching behind them in green and brown.

dialogue.speaker: jivaka_komarabhacca
dialogue.text: “Revered sir, I find no plant without medicinal use.”

i18n.hi: “गुरुदेव, मुझे ऐसा कोई पौधा नहीं मिला जिसका औषधीय उपयोग न हो।”

panels.shot: close-up on teacher’s approving face with Jivaka blurred behind
panels.action: The teacher’s lined face softens into a quiet smile as he glances back toward Jivaka, who stands respectfully a step behind.

dialogue.text: The tale does not list every remedy. It marks an attitude: in that age, attentive healers saw medicine in nearly all of nature, guided by experience, community practice and the ambition to leave nothing unused.

i18n.hi: कहानी हर नुस्खा नहीं गिनती, पर एक दृष्टि दिखाती है—उस युग में सजग वैद्यों को लगभग हर प्रकृति में औषधि दिखती थी, अनुभव, समाज और कुछ भी बेकार न छोड़ने की चाह से मार्गदर्शित।

panels.shot: symbolic mid-shot of parting at a city gate
panels.action: At Takshashila’s gate, the teacher places a hand on Jivaka’s shoulder as Jivaka prepares to depart, a modest satchel of medicines at his side and the road to the east stretching into the plains.

dialogue.text: After years of training, Jivaka left Takshashila not as a miracle-worker, but as a skilled practitioner. His riches were plants, methods and reputation—the tools with which a poor foundling could serve great powers.

i18n.hi: सालों की शिक्षा के बाद जीवक तक्षशिला से चमत्कारी बाबा नहीं, पर कुशल वैद्य बनकर लौटा। उसकी पूँजी थीं पौधे, तरीके और नाम—वही औज़ार जिनसे एक ग़रीब अनाथ बड़े लोगों की सेवा कर सकता था।

panels.shot: wide of Rajagriha’s city returning hero shot
panels.action: Jivaka enters Rajagriha through its stone gate, mingling with traders and monks; in the distance, palace buildings and monastic dwellings both rise, hinting at the two worlds he will navigate.

dialogue.text: Back in Magadha, Jivaka’s skills reached King Bimbisara, later Ajatashatru, and the community around the Buddha. The same hands touched royal patients and wandering ascetics, bridging court and cloister.

i18n.hi: मगध लौटकर जीवक की कला राजा बिंबिसार, फिर अजातशत्रु और बुद्ध के संगति तक पहुँची। वही हाथ राजदरबार के मरीज़ों और घूमते भिक्षुओं को छूते, राज और विहार के बीच सेतु बन गए।

panels.shot: balanced interior wide showing king’s chamber on one side, monastic cell on the other
panels.action: A split composition: on one side Jivaka attends a ailing king in an ornate chamber; on the other he kneels beside a sick monk in a simple cell, his expression equally focused in both scenes.

dialogue.text: Buddhist sources praise his cures, sometimes with hagiographic glow. Historians read through this light, seeing in Jivaka evidence of organized medical practice woven into royal service and monastic life.

i18n.hi: बौद्ध ग्रंथ उसके इलाजों की खूब तारीफ़ करते हैं, कभी चमत्कारी रोशनी के साथ। इतिहासकार उस चमक के आरपार देखते हैं और जीवक में संगठित चिकित्सा को राजसेवा और संघजीवन में बुना हुआ पाते हैं।

panels.shot: quiet grove wide near a monastery
panels.action: Jivaka walks through a monastic grove, watching monks move silently between trees, his physician’s satchel hanging at his side, thoughtful and composed.

dialogue.text: His story traveled across Pali, Sanskrit and Chinese retellings, reshaped but rooted in one truth: knowledge let an abandoned boy stand beside kings and renunciants alike, using healing to turn rejection into service.

i18n.hi: उसकी कथा पाली, संस्कृत और चीनी रूपों में फैली, रूप बदले पर एक सत्य पर टिके रही—ज्ञान ने एक त्यागे हुए बच्चे को राजाओं और सन्यासियों के साथ खड़ा किया, इलाज के ज़रिए ठुकराहट को सेवा में बदल दिया।

title_i18n.en: The Abandoned Boy Who Became the King's Physician
title_i18n.hi: त्यागा हुआ लड़का जो बना राजा का वैद्य

subtitle_i18n.en: From forsaken infant to healer of kings and monks
subtitle_i18n.hi: छुटा हुआ शिशु, जो बना राजाओं और भिक्षुओं का चिकित्सक
